minutes_text:
Minutes
  Lakewood City Council
  Regular Meeting held
  June 23, 2026

MEETING WAS CALLED TO ORDER at 7:31 p.m. by Mayor Chase in the
Council Chambers at the Civic Center, 5000 Clark Avenue, Lakewood, California.

INVOCATION was offered by Reverend Petero Taufagu, Vai O Le Ola Church

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE was led by Scouting America Cub Scout Pack 134

ROLL CALL: PRESENT: Mayor Cassandra Chase
  Vice Mayor Jeff Wood
  Council Member David Arellano
  Council Member Steve Croft
  Council Member Todd Rogers

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PRESENTATIONS:

Mayor Chase 1) announced that the meeting would be adjourned in memory of
a) Detric Green-Barber; and b) former City Council Member Diane DuBois;
2) highlighted the a) Juneteenth commemoration held on Saturday, June 20, 2026,
at Monte Verde Park; and b) upcoming Lakewood Block Party to be held on
Saturday, June 27, 2026; and 3) recognized Dr. Maria Silva-Palacios on her
appointment to the Los Angeles County Alcohol and Other Drugs Commission.

Council Member Croft extended his condolences to the DuBois family, noting that
Council Member DuBois represented both the City and region on numerous boards
and commissions.

Vice Mayor Wood extended his condolences to the DuBois family, further
describing Council Member DuBois as a mentor in regional leadership whose
legacy will continue to benefit the City.

Council Member Rogers 1) extended condolences to the DuBois family, noting that
Council Member DuBois was part of the generation that helped build the Lakewood
community and was a fierce advocate for the City; and 2) regarding the
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) incident near the Lakewood Sheriff’s
Station, stated that the City was unaware of the incident until after it occurred,
further explaining that the City has contacted federal officials to obtain additional
information.
 City Council Minutes
June 23, 2026
Page 2

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PRESENTATIONS – Continued

Council Member Arellano 1) extended condolences to the DuBois family and
thanked Council Member DuBois for her years of service to the City; 2) regarding
the ICE incident, a) reiterated that the City was not aware of the incident until after
it occurred; b) commended the Los Angeles County Fire Department for rendering
aid during the incident; and c) expressed frustration regarding the lack of
communication from federal officials, reiterating that the City continues to seek
additional information; 3) expressed appreciation to the residents who rendered
aid to those involved in a vehicle collision on Del Amo Boulvard; and 4) noted that
this would be Council Member Croft’s final full City Council meeting and presented
him a gift on behalf of the City Council.

For the record, relative to the ICE incident, City Manager McCormack 1) reiterated
that the City was unaware of the incident until after it occurred; and 2) confirmed
that the City contacted Representative Garcia’s office to obtain additional
information and was advised to submit a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)
request, which staff will do.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON ITEMS IN THE AGENDA:

Bill Baca, resident, expressed concerns relative to Item 3.1 (Annual Streets and
Alley Resurfacing and Traffic Calming Pilot Project Findings and
Recommendations), stating that 1) stops signs have been effective in calming
traffic, expressing the opinion that the proposed improvements are inconvenient;
2) the survey data appeared incomplete, noting that although he lives near
Palo Verde Avenue and Candlewood Street, he did not receive a survey; and
3) the City should conduct a more comprehensive study involving residents directly
affected, further requesting that the item be “tabled” for thirty to sixty days.

Philip Norris, resident, spoke in support of Item 3.1 (Annual Streets and Alley
Resurfacing and Traffic Calming Pilot Project Findings and Recommendations),
1) expressing the opinion that the traffic circles have been effective; and
2) requested the City consider a) modifying the bicycle lane striping on Palo Verde
Avenue and Del Amo Boulevard to provide clear lane delineation, similar to the
cities of Long Beach and Cerritos; b) widening the parking lanes on Palo Verde
Avenue as “motor trucks” exceeding the width permitted by City Ordinance
regularly use the roadway; and c) installing traffic circles at the intersections of
Palo Verde Avenue and Harvey Way, and Harvey Way and Los Coyotes Diagonal,
to help alleviate traffic congestion.

Mark Cooper, resident, spoke in support of Item 3.1 (Annual Streets and Alley
Resurfacing and Traffic Calming Pilot Project Findings and Recommendations),
stating that 1) the temporary improvements along Palo Verde Avenue have
reduced speeding and improved driveway access for residents; and 2) traffic
circles generally improve safety as drivers are more likely to navigate them at
slower speeds than run through stop signs.

It was moved by Vice Mayor Wood, seconded by Council Member Arellano, and

1.1 ADOPTION OF 2025 URBAN WATER MANAGEMENT PLAN AND WATER
SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN.

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Director of Water Resources Nguyen 1) provided a PowerPoint presentation of the
Agenda report; and 2) along with City Manager McCormack, responded to
Council Members’ questions and comments.

For the record, 1) Council Member Croft thanked staff for their work, noting the
importance of maintaining eligibility for grant funding, and expressed support for
the recommendation; and 2) Vice Mayor Wood expressed the opinion that
Lakewood has one of the best water departments in the region, highlighting the
City’s well-maintained infrastructure and reliable water supply.

Following discussion, Mayor Chase opened the public hearing at 8:25 p.m. and
called for anyone in the audience wishing to address the City Council on the matter.

Ben Chavez, resident, expressed concern regarding residents served by
Golden State Water Company and questioned whether the proposed plan would
result in additional costs for those customers.

In response to the comments provided by Ben Chavez, 1) Mayor Chase suggested
he speak with Director of Water Resources Ngyuen; and 2) City Manager
McCormack clarified that the Lakewood Municipal Water Utility does not bill
Golden State Water Company customers, further explaining that portions of the
City continue to receive service from Golden State Water Company based on
historical service boundaries established at incorporation.

There being no one else in the audience wishing to address the City Council on
the matter, Mayor Chase closed the public hearing at 8:29 p.m.

For the record, it was moved by Council Member Croft, seconded by
Vice Mayor Wood, and unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to
1) adopt Resolution No. 2026-31 for the 2025 Urban Water Management Plan and
Water Shortage Contingency Plan; and 2) authorize staff to submit adopted 2025
Urban Water Management Plan and Water Shortage Contingency Plan to State
Department of Water Resources:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase

June 23, 2026

3.1 ANNUAL STREETS AND ALLEY RESURFACING AND TRAFFIC CALMING
PILOT PROJECT FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS.

For the record, 1) Mayor Chase introduced the item; and 2) City Manager
McCormack noted that the item had been discussed during the 6:00 p.m.
Study Session held in the Executive Board Room.

Director of Public Works Pickler 1) provided a PowerPoint presentation of the
Agenda report; and 2) along with City Manager McCormack, responded to
Council Members’ questions and comments.

For the record, 1) Council Member Rogers a) thanked staff for their work, noting
that the survey results demonstrated community support for retaining the traffic
calming improvements; b) stated that the pilot project was initiated in response to
concerns regarding pedestrian safety, speeding, and aggressive driving, and
noted that the evaluation demonstrated reductions in those concerns; and
c) suggested conducting additional public outreach regarding the final project
design to provide residents with a greater sense of ownership; and
2) Council Member Arellano thanked staff for their efforts, stating that the
improvements were developed in response to longstanding traffic safety concerns
expressed by residents.

Following discussion, Director Pickler 1) explained that refinements to the
permanent design at Palo Verde Avenue could include a) relocation of the
northbound bus stop at Candlewood Street; b) modifying Candlewood Street to
one lane in each direction near Carfax Avenue; c) minor modifications to the
roundabout; and d) revisions to signage along the project corridor, as needed; and
2) explained that refinements to the permanent design at Studebaker Road could
include a) installation of mountable curbs and hardscaped roundabouts;
b) adjustments to the roundabouts to better accommodate trucks, buses, and other
large vehicles; c) additional signage and pavement markings to improve driver
guidance; d) improved access for landscaping maintenance and street sweeping;
e) modifications to parking lot geometry to reduce vehicle speeds; and
f) construction of Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) compliant curb ramps.

For the record, 1) Council Member Croft thanked staff for their work and noted that
the Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Committee reviewed the traffic analysis
and survey results and recommended proceeding with the proposed
improvements; 2) Vice Mayor Wood a) stated that change often creates confusion
but emphasized that public education is important and that the improvements
would enhance traffic safety; and b) suggested evaluating the effects of the project
on nearby arterial streets; and 3) Mayor Chase commended staff for their
responsiveness in refining the project based on resident feedback, reiterating that
the CIP Committee supported moving forward with the proposed modifications.

June 23, 2026

3.1 ANNUAL STREETS AND ALLEY RESURFACING AND TRAFFIC CALMING
PILOT PROJECT FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS – Continued

In response to questions and comments provided by Council Member Rogers and
Vice Mayor Wood, City Manager McCormack confirmed that staff could conduct
additional outreach regarding the final design and evaluate potential impacts on
surrounding arterial streets.

Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Croft, seconded by
Council Member Arellano, and unanimously carried by the following roll call vote,
to 1) find that the Palo Verde Avenue and Studebaker Road Traffic Calming
Projects have successfully achieved the intended traffic calming and safety
objectives and approve the incorporation of the recommended refinements
identified through the pilot evaluation process; and 2) authorize staff to proceed
with final design and construction of the permanent traffic calming improvements
at Palo Verde Avenue and Studebaker Road utilizing the previously approved
funding and construction authorizations and incorporating modifications identified
through the pilot program evaluation:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase

3.2 UPDATE TO LAKEWOOD’S MASTER TREE LIST AND TREE PLANTING
PLAN.

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Director of Public Works Pickler 1) provided a verbal report of the Agenda report;
and 2) along with Tree and Hardscape Supervisor Hunt, responded to
Council Members’ questions and comments.

For the record, 1) Council Member Croft noted that the proposed updates continue
the City’s longstanding efforts to reduce sidewalk damage while maintaining its
Tree City USA designation; 2) Council Member Rogers stated that maintaining the
Tree City USA designation is an important achievement and that the proposed
updates balance preservation of the City’s urban forest with the flexibility needed
to address changing conditions; and 3) Mayor Chase commented that trees
continue to enhance the City’s health, sustainability, and quality of life, further
expressing appreciation for the City’s continued commitment to tree planting.

At the request of Vice Mayor Wood, Director Pickler confirmed that the Master Tree
List and Tree Planting Plan would be made available on the City’s website.
 City Council Minutes
June 23, 2026
Page 7

3.2 UPDATE TO LAKEWOOD’S MASTER TREE LIST AND TREE PLANTING
PLAN – Continued

It was moved by Council Member Croft, seconded by Vice Mayor Wood, and
unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to adopt the updated Master
Tree List, Tree Planting Plan, and Residential Parkway Tree Policy dated
June 23, 2026:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase

3.3 RESOLUTION NO. 2026-32 – DECLARING JULY AS PARKS MAKE LIFE
BETTER! MONTH.

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Director of Recreation and Community Services Frost 1) provided a PowerPoint
presentation of the Agenda report; and 2) responded to Council Members’
questions and comments.

For the record, 1) Vice Mayor Wood emphasized the important role Recreation and
Community Services plays in enhancing residents’ daily lives through its programs
and active and passive recreational spaces; 2) Council Member Rogers
highlighted that the City allocates nearly equal levels of funding to Public Safety,
Public Works, and Recreation and Community Services, reflecting the City of
Lakewood’s longstanding commitment to maintaining a high quality of life; and
3) Mayor Chase reiterated that Recreation and Community Services provides
opportunities for residents of all ages to participate in programs and activities that
strengthen the community.

In response to questions and comments provided by Council Member Arellano,
Director Frost reported that approximately 1,500 youth athletes attended the
Lakewood Youth Sports Opening Day ceremonies, representing the highest
attendance since before the COVID-19 pandemic.

Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Croft, seconded by
Council Member Arellano, and unanimously carried by the following roll call vote,
to adopt Resolution No. 2026-32:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase

3.4 AMENDMENT NO. 5 TO AGREEMENT FOR EMPLOYMENT OF CITY
MANAGER.

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Deputy City Attorney Skolnik provided a verbal report of the Agenda report.

For the record, Council Member Arellano thanked City Manager McCormack for
his leadership and service to the City.

It was moved by Vice Mayor Wood, seconded by Council Member Croft, and
unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to approve Amendment No. 5
to Agreement for Employment of City Manager:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase

For the record, City Manager McCormack thanked the City Council for their
continued leadership and support, noting that it is an honor to serve the
community.

LAKEWOOD HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY

1 REGISTER OF DEMANDS

It was moved by Council Member Rogers, seconded by Council Member Arellano,
and unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to approve the register of
demands:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

Brittni Reyes, Helpline Youth Counseling, 1) stated that she is a representative
of Helpline Youth Counseling, a non-profit organization that promotes individual,
family, and community health, well-being, prosperity, and equity; 2) explained that
the South East Community Alliance (SECA) administers prevention and
community safety initiatives, including the safe disposal of unused medications,
noting that SECA has partnered with four pharmacies in the City of Lakewood to
provide convenient medication drop-off locations; and 3) encouraged the City to
partner with SECA to expand access to safe medication disposal sites.
 City Council Minutes
June 23, 2026
Page 9

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS – Continued

Philip Norris, resident, 1) asked how many full-time employees are dedicated to
homeless services, what metrics are used to determine staffing levels, and how
many contacts staff make with individuals experiencing homelessness each
month; 2) stated that a comparison between the Cerritos Sheriff's Station and the
Cypress Police Department indicated the latter costs approximately half as much,
further questioning whether the City of Lakewood has conducted a similar
comparison; 3) questioned whether the Recreation and Community Services
Department offers programs addressing issues affecting young men; and 4) stated
that links included in recent City Council agendas do not function on Android
devices.

Bill Baca, resident, extended condolences to the DuBois family, stating that her
passing is a significant loss to the City.

Dr. Ahmed Rafi, resident, 1) extended condolences to the DuBois family;
2) expressed gratitude to the City and local nonprofit organizations for their support
following the passing of his wife; 3) thanked Council Member Rogers and
Council Member Croft for the opportunity to serve on the Measure L Citizens
Oversight Committee; and 4) requested that the City minimize the loss of street
parking and residential privacy associated with Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs).

Gisela Nily, resident, 1) expressed concern regarding the current political
environment and public complacency; and 2) suggested installing cameras in front
of City Hall and the Lakewood Sheriff's Station.

Susan Singer, resident, expressed concerns regarding the recent ICE incident
near the Lakewood Sheriff's Station, stating that 1) she does not feel safe in the
community; 2) Lakewood Indivisible has peacefully advocated for civil rights,
democracy, and nonviolence; 3) she watched a video of the incident and was
horrified; and 4) other incidents have occurred outside the Lakewood Sheriff's
Station but have gone largely unnoticed.

Heather Rodrigez, resident, expressed concerns regarding the recent ICE
incident near the Lakewood Sheriff’s Station, stating that 1) she appreciates the
City’s investigation into the matter; 2) had the incident not been recorded, residents
may not have known it occurred or been able to identify the individual to offer
assistance; 3) the City and Lakewood Sheriff’s Station should consider measures
to mitigate potential public safety concerns associated with ICE activities occurring
near public facilities, noting that the Sheriff’s Department should be aware when
use of force incidents occur immediately outside the station; 4) Sheriff’s Deputies
can serve as witnesses and help deescalate situations; 5) the City should consider
establishing “ICE free zones” through a City Council Resolution and ensure City
staff and Sheriff’s personnel monitor those areas; and 6) the City and Sheriff’s
Department should work collaboratively on strategies moving forward.
 City Council Minutes
June 23, 2026
Page 10

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS – Continued

Kay Ewing Donato, resident, read a poem regarding ICE.

Anna Pinnolis, expressed concerns regarding the ICE incident near the
Lakewood Sheriff's Station, stating that 1) officers were not in danger and the
individual being detained was complying with commands; 2) although the City has
remained neutral regarding immigration enforcement, the incident occurring
directly outside of the Sheriff's Station adjacent to City Hall does not reflect that
neutrality; and 3) the City Council should consider adopting a Resolution
establishing “ICE free zones” within municipal buildings, where ICE agents would
be denied access without a warrant.

Vanesha Davis, resident, expressed concerns regarding ADUs and parking,
stating that 1) ADUs have negatively impacted residents' quality of life by reducing
available street parking; 2) while she understands the City must comply with State
mandates, the impacts of reduced parking on residents have not been adequately
addressed; 3) she is now required to park farther from her home, creating safety
concerns; and 4) residents without driveways should be allowed to install them
where feasible to alleviate the parking issues.

In response to comments provided by Vanesha Davis, Mayor Chase suggested
she speak with Director of Community Development Cervantes.

Stephanie Tellonez, resident, expressed concerns regarding the ICE incident
near the Lakewood Sheriff's Station, stating that 1) she appreciates the City's
investigation into the matter; 2) public trust is undermined by ICE activities,
expressing the opinion that trust is essential for civic participation and cooperation;
and 3) while she is proud of the community, the City should preserve that trust by
welcoming public scrutiny of how incidents are addressed.

Matthew Mikuri, resident, expressed concerns regarding the ICE incident near
the Lakewood Sheriff's Station, stating that 1) ICE engages in harassment and
racial profiling of residents; 2) the incident occurred in the Sheriff's Station parking
lot adjacent to City Hall; however, a public statement has not been issued
acknowledging it; 3) the incident raises broader public safety concerns; and 4) the
City Council should take action.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business to be brought before the City Council,
Mayor Chase adjourned the meeting at 9:54 p.m. to Tuesday, July 14, 2026, at
7:00 p.m. in the Weingart Ballroom. A moment of silence was observed in memory
of Detric Green-Barber and Diane Dubois.

Respectfully submitted,

Dakota Wallace, CMC
City Clerk
